smell_validity.evidence: The injection embodies the smell in four authentic shapes: flag-guarded branches over permanently false constants, statements stranded after unconditional raises, and helper, registry and import names serving only those branches. Deadness is statically certain; dormant variants shadow live policy in delivery, commit and compilation paths, so the practical cost and the boundary from healthy design are unmistakable without the label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Every live policy in the touched modules now carries a dormant twin to read past or keep coherent—constructors, notification delivery, recycling, parameter and default resolution, row access, commit—and unreachable corpses misdocument the rejected operations. Removal makes future work safer and shorter, but the gain stays within existing methods; no larger responsibility boundary is restored.

development_plausibility.evidence: The residue mirrors transitions this driver plausibly underwent—explicit loop adoption, listener-era notify delivery, sync-method rejection conversions, SQLAlchemy 1.4 execution rules—with matching placement, provenance comments and helper idiom, so it reads as a release flag left behind. Only the uniform switch naming and parallel comment structure hint at construction.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The prompt names both layers and every remnant family, fixes the finished state (retired branches, corpses, switches, registries, aliases, including ordinary-looking import names), the preservation boundary (public API, signatures, error messages, runtime behavior list), and bars partial cleanup, revival and unrelated restructuring. It decisively prevents costly leftovers, over-deletion and adjacent redesign while leaving implementation freedom.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Purposes genuinely differ: loop adoption, notify routing, recycle auditing, sync-rejection corpses, parameter distillation, default resolution, row access and commit semantics. Repairs require three different decisions—constant-permanence analysis, post-raise reachability, and sole-consumer name-liveness across modules. Score four, not five: every repair action is still plain deletion.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names remnant families but not locations. Configuration-selected import-time router registration must be combined with registry-lookup dispatch inside the delivery loop to bound one removal group; helper usage plus import aliases cross three modules; live lookalikes—rejection stubs, surviving loop helpers in the rewritten import block, the live prefetch merge—must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: Each retired path is a cross-file group under one shared removal rule: deleting a switch alone breaks import or instantiation; deleting only branches leaves orphan constants, helpers and import lines the completion criteria forbid. Dependencies run one direction and deletions stay order-free, so no second interacting rule emerges.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: One uniform sweep over the disabled-flag family deletes every guarded branch and its constant outright—most injected locations—with a single behavior-preservation argument and no per-site behavioral decision. Corpse removal and name-liveness work behind orphan helpers, the registry and import aliases are separate operations; the single rule still clears the 60-80 percent band.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Two hidden paths exist: a behavior-preserving partial cleanup—an orphan helper or import surviving—provably keeps results identical, so no behavioral run can flag it; and reviving or mis-cutting a stranded after-raise region passes ordinary calls and changes only special-state error handling, with the near-duplicate dormant/live compiler pair inviting a wrong choice.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
